record.paper_title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: For the Lieb-Thirring eigenvalue-moment inequality sum_n |E_n(-Δ+V)|^γ ≤ L_{γ,d} ∫_{R^d} V_-(x)^(γ+d/2) dx, determine the optimal constant L_{γ,d} for every admissible pair (γ,d), namely γ≥1/2 when d=1, γ>0 when d=2, and γ≥0 when d≥3.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11. Find the optimal constants Lγ,d in (19).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 1$ and let $V:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be a real-valued potential with negative part $V_-(x)=\max(-V(x),0)$ such that $V_-\in L^{\gamma+d/2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Consider the Schrödinger operator $H=-\Delta+V$ acting on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, and let $E_1(H)\le E_2(H)\le\cdots<0$ denote its negative eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity).

For an admissible pair $(\gamma,d)$, namely
- $\gamma\ge 1/2$ if $d=1$,
- $\gamma>0$ if $d=2$,
- $\gamma\ge 0$ if $d\ge 3$,

the Lieb–Thirring inequality asserts the existence of a finite constant $L_{\gamma,d}>0$ such that
$$\sum_n |E_n(-\Delta+V)|^{\gamma}\;\le\; L_{\gamma,d}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} V_-(x)^{\gamma+d/2}\,dx$$
for every such $V$. Determine the optimal (smallest admissible) value of the constant $L_{\gamma,d}$ for every admissible pair $(\gamma,d)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The optimal constants are known only in two regimes: $d=1$ with $\gamma=1/2$ (Hundertmark–Lieb–Thomas) and all $d\ge 1$ with $\gamma\ge 3/2$ (Laptev–Weidl, agreeing with the semiclassical Weyl constant). For all other admissible pairs the optimal value of $L_{\gamma,d}$ remains unknown. Recent work has shown that, contrary to the original Lieb–Thirring conjecture, in dimensions $d\ge 2$ the optimum is not attained at the one–bound–state case for $\gamma>\max(0,2-d/2)$, so the structure of extremizers is more subtle than originally believed; the problem is therefore open in general.

status_evidence.title: The state of the Lieb–Thirring conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: the cases d = 1, γ = 1/2 and d ≥ 1, γ ≥ 3/2 are the only parameter regions where the conjecture is proved and the only regions where the optimal constant is known
status_evidence.claim: Optimal constants are only known in two specific regimes; the problem is open elsewhere.

status_evidence.title: The Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation for Orthonormal Functions II
status_evidence.snippet: the best Lieb–Thirring constant when the eigenvalues are raised to the power κ is never given by the one-bound state case when κ > max(0,2-d/2) in dimension d ≥ 1
status_evidence.claim: Part of the original Lieb–Thirring conjecture about the form of optimizers has been disproved in dimensions d≥2.
